cards.name: Note
cards.text: The specific user problem this design solves, in one sentence. If you can't state it in one sentence, the scope probably isn't settled yet — get that answer before wireframing anything.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Key findings from user interviews/surveys — pain points and needs this design should actually address, not assumed ones. A quote from a real user carries more weight here than a design team's intuition.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Screenshots of competitor products with SPECIFIC notes on what works and what doesn't (not just "theirs looks nice") — what flow do they use, where do users likely get stuck, what would you copy vs. deliberately avoid.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: The core user flow(s) this design needs to support, start to finish, before any visual design begins. A beautiful screen that sits in the wrong place in the flow still fails the user.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Rough layout and hierarchy only, no color or final type — verify the LAYOUT solves the flow before investing in visual polish. Changing a wireframe costs minutes; changing a finished high-fidelity screen costs hours.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Interfaces whose visual language (component style, spacing, typography feel, not necessarily function) you want to draw from for the high-fidelity pass.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Color palette, type scale, spacing units, and component states (default/hover/active/disabled/error) locked here as the single source of truth — every screen built after this references these tokens, never a one-off value.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Contrast ratio targets (WCAG AA minimum: 4.5:1 for body text), keyboard-navigation requirements, and screen-reader considerations designed in from the start — retrofitting accessibility after launch costs far more than building it in from the wireframe stage.

cards.name: Note
cards.text: Drop competitor screenshots, user-research clips (video), and interview notes (image or file cards) here — "research before you design the screen" only works if the research is actually on the board.

connections.note: The problem statement scopes the user research
Research informs the user flow/information architecture
Competitive analysis informs the user flow
The flow/IA becomes the low-fidelity wireframes
Visual/UI references inform the design system tokens
Accessibility constraints shape the wireframes/flow — a real cross-cutting dependency, not an afterthought
Design system tokens style the wireframe/flow implementation
Screenshots and user research feed the research notes
